xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-1610: Consistent issue actions across all surfaces (Command Deck cockpit, Pipeline rows, Board cards, IssueDrawer)

plan.title: Consistent issue actions across all surfaces (Command Deck cockpit, Pipeline rows, Board cards, IssueDrawer)
plan.author: agent:claude-fable-5

narratives.Problem: After the Command Deck remodel, an issue appears on several surfaces (cockpit, pipeline rows, board cards, drawer, rail, Zone B) but each surface owns its own action rendering: the cockpit mega menu keeps a bespoke GROUP_ORDER mapping, the board/drawer hybrid toolbar has a flat non-grouped overflow plus a bolted MergeButton, the board hardcodes an Unpause button, the rail passes ad-hoc sessionExtras, and Zone B hardcodes every mutation. What you can do to an issue depends on where you look at it, and nothing stops the surfaces drifting further apart.
narratives.Proposal: Finish the PAN-2661 registry consolidation per the binding PRD rev 2: extract the grouped menu body from the Radix context-menu chrome into a shared component; give IssueActionMenu declared presentation modes (primary-strip with '⋯ N more' grouped overflow, overflow-only grouped, typed pins including the drawer's pinned MergeButton component slot); promote session/non-issue action metadata into an executable discriminated-union contract and migrate the rail extras and the Zone B strip onto it; converge the cockpit panel on the shared body; then lock it all with a six-surface parity test built on an explicit expectedActions oracle. Surfaces contribute only { mode, pinned?, context }; the registry owns everything else.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No changes to action semantics, endpoints, or server routes for existing ISSUE_ACTIONS entries (PRD D-5)
- merge is NOT promoted to a registry key and MergeButton is NOT deleted (supersedes the stale 2026-06-04 spec approach)
- No new issue-scoped actions (no issue-level viewVbrief catalog entry; Zone B viewVbrief stays session-scoped)
- No dashboard-to-CLI parity work (that axis is PAN-243)
- No visual restyling beyond the declared presentation modes; style-guide tokens only
- No new Mintlify page for action menus (none exists today; verified 2026-07-15 — stated, not omitted)
- No behavior changes to the 'inline' agent-scope mode consumers beyond mode-name compatibility

autoDecisions.summary: Superseded the 2026-06-04 spec (merge-as-registry-key, delete-MergeButton approach) with a fresh item set.
autoDecisions.rationale: That spec predates PAN-2499/PAN-2661 and directly contradicts the operator-reviewed PRD rev 2 correction D-3 (merge stays a pinned MergeButton component, not a registry key). No old item survives semantically, so old item IDs were not preserved. The dead agent's 2-line uncommitted diff implementing the old spec must be reverted (recorded as hazard H1).

autoDecisions.summary: Split PRD work item 2 (board + drawer) into two vBRIEF items and numbered Zone B migration as its own item.
autoDecisions.rationale: Decomposition guidance: one focused, independently reviewable change per item. Zone B promotion is required by PRD D-2/FR-1/FR-5 even though the PRD's work-item list does not number it separately.

autoDecisions.summary: Covered Pipeline rows via the shared IssueActionMenu 'overflow-only' mode and included them as a sixth render point in the parity test.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue title names Pipeline rows as a surface but the PRD's five-surface enumeration omits them; PipelineView.tsx:245 consumes IssueActionMenu mode='overflow-only', so upgrading that mode's overflow to the grouped body converges pipeline rows without editing PipelineView, and the parity test locks it.

autoDecisions.summary: Renamed mode 'hybrid' to 'primary-strip' while keeping 'overflow-only' and 'inline'.
autoDecisions.rationale: PRD D-3 says the hybrid toolbar becomes primary-strip mode; keeping the other mode names avoids touching agent-scope consumers (FleetAgentsView etc.) outside this issue's scope.

autoDecisions.summary: PAN-2499 inventory/no-loss updates land inside each conversion item's commit rather than batched in the docs item.
autoDecisions.rationale: The no-loss gate runs per commit; batching relocations at the end would leave intermediate commits red, violating the independently-mergeable rule. The docs item verifies the final relocated-never-removed state.

Extract the body into a new shared component (suggested name IssueActionGroupedBody) that is parametrized over its item primitives (an adapter prop with {Item, DestructiveItem, Label, Separator} implementations, or an equivalent plain-button implementation plus a context-menu adapter) so the identical body renders inside (a) the Radix context menu on the rail, (b) a click-popover (cockpit, later item), and (c) an overflow popover (board/drawer/pipeline, later item). GroupedIssueActionMenu becomes a thin ContextMenu wrapper composing the shared body; the rail's rendered structure must not change. Keep the sessionExtras prop working for now (it is deleted in register-rail-extras). Do NOT touch cockpit/board/drawer in this item.

narrative.Action: Per PRD D-3 and the binding mockup (docs/design/mockups/issue-actions-one-registry-pan-1610.html): rename IssueActionMenu mode 'hybrid' to 'primary-strip'. In primary-strip, keep the phase-primary inline buttons and replace the flat OverflowMenu with the shared grouped body (from extract-grouped-body) opened from the overflow trigger, which gains a text label of the form '⋯ N more' (N = number of non-primary actions). In 'overflow-only' mode, render the same grouped body with zero inline primaries — PipelineView.tsx:245 consumes overflow-only unchanged and thereby receives the grouped overflow (do not edit PipelineView.tsx). Keep 'inline' mode and agentScopeOnly behavior untouched. Extend the pin API: pinRight registry-key pins keep working (DrawerActionBar uses pinRight=['viewPr']); add a typed pinned-component slot — e.g. pinned: [{ key: 'merge', render: <component> }] — rendered as a declared component excluded from overflow and from set-parity (D-3 amendment to D-1). Update all mode-name references ('hybrid') across the frontend in this item so typecheck stays green.

Promote session/non-issue action metadata into an executable contract (one schema, two scopes)

metadata.parallelSafeReason: Wave-0 foundation; sole owner of issueActions.ts until its dependents start — both are serialized behind it via blocks edges.

narrative.Action: Per PRD D-2: extend issueActions.ts so session-scoped and non-issue entries get the full executable shape (availability predicate, invocation, description, kind, confirm spec) via a discriminated union sharing one schema with ISSUE_ACTIONS — discriminated by scope. Reuse the EXISTING union values: NonIssueActionScope ('project' | 'container' | 'session-artifact' | 'agent-state' | 'session') and ownerSurface ('ProjectNode' | 'ContainerNode' | 'FeatureItem' | 'ZoneBActionStrip'); extend those unions if needed, never invent parallel ones. Invocation must accept a surface-provided context object (session id, issue id, and UI callbacks such as onViewTerminal) because several session actions are UI callbacks, not endpoints. This item is schema + entry promotion only — it must be additive: no surface changes consumers yet (rail migrates in register-rail-extras, Zone B in migrate-zoneb-strip). Session-scope keys must remain OUT of the issue-scoped ISSUE_ACTIONS array; the no-actions-lost test premises that separation and must keep enforcing it.

items.title: issueActions.ts contains a discriminated-union action schema in which session/non-issue entries carry the executable shape (availability predicate, invocation, description, kind, confirm) alongside ISSUE_ACTIONS — one schema covering two scopes, reusing the existing ownerSurface and scope union values
issueActions.no-actions-lost.test.ts passes with its separation premise intact: ZONE_B_SESSION_ACTIONS and PROJECT_TREE_CONTEXT_ACTIONS keys stay absent from ISSUE_ACTIONS proper
npm run typecheck exits with zero errors and every rendered surface preserves its current behavior (the promotion is additive; surfaces migrate in later items)
Convert Kanban board cards to primary-strip mode and migrate the hardcoded Unpause button to the registry

Per PRD D-5 board note: KanbanCards.tsx:615-628 defines a local handleUnpause fetch to POST /api/agents/:id/unpause and renders a hardcoded '▶ Unpause' button (:745-750); delete the local handler/button and route Unpause through the registry 'unpause' entry (same endpoint — behavior-neutral), preserving the success toast and dashboard refresh. NFR-1: the card strip keeps its current width budget — phase primaries plus the overflow trigger only; the overflow absorbs everything else. If any PAN-2499 inventory 'home' for a board section changes, update inventory.ts/densitySections.ts in the same commit.

Delete the side-by-side MergeButton composition; merge renders via the declaration. Update the PAN-2499 inventory entry for DrawerActionBar in the same commit if its home changes.

narrative.Action: Per PRD glossary + D-2: ZONE_B_SESSION_ACTIONS (issueActions.ts:149-155) is metadata-only while ZoneBActionStrip.tsx hardcodes its own mutations (kill/suspend/resume/restart/replay/deep-wipe fetches, confirm dialogs at :131/:146/:173, overflow items at :355-395). The strip keeps its compact visual layout (inline stop/terminal/pause-resume + overflow) but renders labels, confirmation flows, and invocations from the contract and defines none of its own — hardcoded behavior preserved verbatim (D-5), including the stop-session confirmation copy, the codex-blocked spawn handling, toasts, and refreshes. Cross-surface action-parity test built on an explicit per-surface oracle

narrative.Action: Per FR-5: create src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/__tests__/issue-actions-surface-parity.test.tsx with an explicit oracle function expectedActions(registry, state, surface, context). Surfaces legitimately differ (session extras on rail/Zone B, pinned merge on drawer), so parity means each surface's rendered output ≡ its oracle output — not surface ≡ surface. Render six surfaces: cockpit panel, rail context menu, board card strip, drawer strip, pipeline row overflow (overflow-only mode as consumed by PipelineView), and Zone B strip. Assert by introspecting rendered output: action set identity, enabled/disabled gating identity, danger-last ordering, and zero out-of-registry MENU items (pinned component slots exempt per D-3 but asserted present via the pin declaration). Include negative fixtures proving the comparator detects each drift class. Note the existing issueActions.parity.test.tsx covers the registry↔CLI axis (PAN-243) — leave it in place; this file is the cross-surface axis.

items.title: The new file src/dashboard/frontend/src/lib/__tests__/issue-actions-surface-parity.test.tsx creates an explicit oracle expectedActions(registry, state, surface, context) and derives every expectation from it
